=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:209 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fallback regex for GitHub closing keywords is incomplete and can miss valid closing references or match invalid substrings/forms.
  WHY: Reviewers disagree on intent, but the highest severity is medium; one reviewer notes the regex only includes `closes|fixes|resolves`, another notes GitHub also accepts `close|closed|fix|fixed|resolve|resolved`, and another flags lack of word boundaries/zero-separator matching that can create false positives.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:276-293 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL batch validation treats an all-null aliased response as success instead of falling back conservatively.
  WHY: All reviewers agree the jq success path does not ensure meaningful issue data was extracted; if every aliased lookup is null, the workflow can skip REST fallback and incorrectly proceed as if no orchestrator-managed issues exist.
- tests/test_issue_pr_status_payload_fallback_contract.py:49 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The regression test asserts the current fallback-regex string literally.
  WHY: If the workflow regex is expanded, this test must be updated in lockstep or CI will fail.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
(No findings reported.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:209 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fallback regex for GitHub closing keywords is incomplete.
  WHY: It only includes `closes`, `fixes`, and `resolves`, so valid forms like `fixed #123` can be missed when the primary GraphQL field is empty.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:276-291 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL batch validation does not verify that at least one aliased issue lookup returned a non-null value.
  WHY: If every aliased issue is null, the workflow can treat the batch as successful and incorrectly apply labels or close issues.
- tests/test_issue_pr_status_payload_fallback_contract.py:49 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The regression test strictly asserts the presence of the incomplete regex.
  WHY: Updating the workflow regex without updating the test will fail CI.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:209 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback regex only matches three of GitHub's nine supported closing keywords and includes an optional colon that GitHub doesn't recognize in auto-linking.
  WHY: If a PR uses a supported keyword outside `closes|fixes|resolves`, or the colon variant, the fallback path will not detect the linked issue.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:280-293 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL success path does not guard against the case where all aliased issue lookups return null.
  WHY: The batch can be treated as successful with empty extracted issues, which can bypass the skip guard and reintroduce incorrect labeling/closing.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:275-293 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Empty jq result treated as success, potentially missing orchestrator issues.
  WHY: The inner check only validates jq exit code, not whether meaningful data was extracted, so partial GraphQL data can be misclassified as success.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:275-293 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The inner if only validates that jq didn't error, not that meaningful data was extracted.
  WHY: This can lead to false negatives in edge cases where GraphQL returns valid structure but incomplete data.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:209 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The regex only matches plural forms, but GitHub also accepts singular and past-tense closing keywords.
  WHY: This may miss legitimate closing references, though the reviewer explicitly says it is an intentional conservative choice and not a blocker.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:209 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The closing-keyword pattern lacks word boundaries before the keyword and allows zero separator characters between the keyword and `#`.
  WHY: This can match substrings inside other words and invalid forms like `closes#123`, causing false-positive issue extraction.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:276-290 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The jq extraction block checks only the jq exit status, not whether any issue numbers were actually extracted.
  WHY: If all aliased issue nodes are null, the workflow can skip REST fallback and proceed as if orchestrator-managed issues were absent.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
